rationale:
Evidence: iteration 10 (outer sensors at x = -0.04 and +0.04, y = 0.06; inner three at y = 0.03; kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, line_loss last_direction, sensor_size 0.012) is the best raced design at 234.2, with 9 of 20 oval completions and oval progress of 0.84. Every step from it since then has lowered the score: base_speed 1.8 gave 136.1 with every run off track, and ki 0.15 gave 171.9 with oval progress 0.66, below the 0.70 threshold. Line loss stayed near 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom in every raced iteration, and no kp, kd, footprint, spread or speed change moved it.

Change: none. This is the final iteration and there is no later race to verify a new single-variable change, so the design that has raced best is the safest candidate for the unseen-track evaluation. The geometry and controller below are identical to iteration 10. The entityR1 approval describes the same build, so it is consistent with this candidate.

Expected result: a score near 234, with oval completions and progress similar to iteration 10. The unseen track is different, so the s-bend and slalom behaviour (progress about 0.17 and 0.11 in iteration 10, with line loss near 1.0) remains the main risk.

Hypotheses: (a) the forward outer sensors (y = 0.06) carry the oval gain to unseen tracks with bend entry similar to the oval. (b) Line loss stays near 1.0 because the failure is turn-in geometry, not controller gain.

Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and noise_robustness on each track, to confirm that the result matches iteration 10.
